reading.body:
Global DC OY is a plausible small Finnish data-center business, not a confirmed one: the name carries a Finnish corporate suffix and a likely "data center" abbreviation, but no capacity, operator, or operating status is verified.

The record is an OpenStreetMap way tagged as a data center, located at 60.63 north, 25.26 east, roughly 24 miles from Helsinki Vantaa Airport. The name itself is the evidence. "OY" is the standard Finnish limited-company suffix, and "DC" most likely stands for data center, a naming pattern real hosting and colocation firms use. That combination makes this the strongest candidate for a genuine facility among the low-information European records reviewed alongside it.

What the data does not contain is the part that matters for AI. There is no megawatt figure, no operator, no website, no confirmed service offering, and no business-registration check. The research status is exhausted, meaning the search quota ran out before confirmation, not that the company was found to be inactive. A reader should treat this as a lead rather than a load.

For the compute thesis, the entry is a reminder about the floor of the data. A facility can exist in a map database with a name and coordinates and still tell you nothing about whether it draws power, how much, or whether it serves AI workloads at all. The binding constraints on AI scaling are measured in megawatts and interconnection queues, and none of that is present here.
